first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, so simplifying onboarding directly addresses both current problems. The archived evidence supports durable gains in completion, time-to-value, and SMB first-week activation. A standard experiment is appropriate, with downstream qualified-revenue and lead-quality checks to ensure higher activation does not come at the expense of sustainable value.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding to address the current 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline. The strongest verified evidence shows improved completion, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention. Include qualified revenue, retention, and segment-level guardrails because signup simplification previously reduced SMB retention by 1% and was not validated outside SMB.

final2.rationale: The new competitor cut and doubled price-sensitive SMB churn conversations create an immediate, segment-specific revenue threat that outweighs the previously selected onboarding optimization for this response decision. Run targeted promotional pricing only for demonstrably price-sensitive SMB prospects or at-risk accounts, with strict limits and guardrails on qualified revenue, retention, gross margin, discount leakage, and post-promotion churn. This is a guarded test rather than a broad price response because the inherited pricing evidence has not been independently verified and discounts can trade short-term acquisition for unsustainable revenue.
